answer: Cap each identity's influence by a river of verifiable work: to join, an agent must complete a stream of small, time-stamped tasks whose results peers can check, and its reputation flows only from that proven history. A lagoon of idle accounts earns nothing, so creating a thousand fakes means paying a thousand times the work. At the zenith of trust sits an agent with a long, checkable record, not the loudest newcomer. Fakes drown in cost before they can vote or trade.
